:::{#exm-vcov-zero-indpt}
#### Independent but not conditionally independent

<!-- no-figure: one 3 x 3 matrix and its inverse; nothing to plot -->

Let $\vX = \tp{(X_1, X_2, X_3)}$ have $\E{\vX} = \matr{0}$ and

$$
\Varf{\vX} = \pmat{1 & 0 & 1/2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1/2 \\ 1/2 & 1/2 & 1}.
$$

The $(1, 2)$ element is 0,
so by @thm-vcov-zero-indpt, $X_1$ and $X_2$ are [independent](independence.qmd#def-indpt).
By @thm-precision-matrix-inverse, the [precision matrix](#def-precision-matrix) is the [inverse](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-special-matrices.html#def-matrix-inverse) of this [matrix](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-matrices.html#def-matrix),

$$
\precision(\vX) = \pmat{3/2 & 1/2 & -1 \\ 1/2 & 3/2 & -1 \\ -1 & -1 & 2},
$$

which one can check by multiplying the two matrices to get $\matr{I}_3$.
Its $(1, 2)$ element is $1/2 \ne 0$,
so by @thm-precision-zero-cind, $X_1$ and $X_2$ are not [conditionally independent given](independence.qmd#def-cind-continuous) $X_3$:
a zero in the [variance matrix](variance-covariance.qmd#def-cov-vec-x) means independence, and a zero in the precision matrix means [conditional independence](independence.qmd#def-cind-continuous),
and neither implies the other.

:::
